text.p: SmithKline Beecham said on Wednesday a clinical trial showed human volunteers were protected against malaria after vaccination with an experimental vaccine developed in collaboration with the U.S. army's Walter Reed Army Institute of Research.
But the company said the final development of a malaria vaccine suitable for broad applications would still require considerable work.
Detailed results of the study are to be published in the New England Journal of Medicine on January 9.
In tests on seven volunteers injected with the experimental vaccine, only one developed malaria. In contrast, all the non-vaccinated volunteers became infected.
A series of clinical trials including a field trial of limited scope in West Africa, is to be initiated in the course of the next few months.
